name: Insulation
summary: Materials that slow heat loss: glass and mineral wool, foam board, spray foam and reflective foil.
uses: Insulating a shelter, room or sleeping area
Building a cooler, hay-box cooker or solar oven
Wrapping pipes and tanks against freezing
identify: Lofts and wall cavities, foam boards on building sites, foam inside fridges, freezers, coolers and water heaters, and foil on HVAC ducts. In old buildings, silver-gold to grey-brown loose-fill vermiculite may contain asbestos (CCOHS vermiculite), and so may old insulation wrapped round pipes (CCOHS asbestos home): leave them alone. Plastic foam left uncovered can let a fire grow fast, its smoke and toxic gases are a serious hazard to people inside, and it needs a covering that limits the heat reaching it (NRC CBD-178): keep it covered and away from stoves and heaters.
test: Dry, fluffy and clean is good; wet, squashed or mouldy insulation has lost most of its value. Wear gloves, long sleeves, eye protection and an N95 mask for glass wool (IDPH fiberglass).

decay.note: Lasts if dry. Wet insulation is useless and grows mould.

sources.title: NRC CBD-178: Shorter GW and McGuire JH, Fire and Plastic Foam Insulation Material, Canadian Building Digest 178 (National Research Council Canada, Division of Building Research, June 1976; NRC Publications Archive, a discontinued series kept as a historical reference)

IDPH fiberglass: Illinois Department of Public Health, Fiberglass
